# Project Presentation (Narrated Deck) {.unnumbered}

## Overview

The term-project presentation is a **narrated 5-7 slide deck submitted online with the [Final Portfolio](../../milestones/final-portfolio/README.md)** on Dec 11. There is no in-class presentation session. The deck is the knowledge-translation version of your project: it should emphasize scientific clarity, knowledge translation, reproducibility, and auditability.

Full requirements and the 10-point rubric are in the [Presentation brief](../../milestones/m5-presentation/README.md); this page is the how-to for recording and submitting it.

## What To Record

Record narration over your slides so a viewer can follow the story without you in the room. Any of these is acceptable:

- a narrated `slides.html` or `slides.pdf` export;
- a short screen recording that walks through the slides with voice-over.

Keep it to the length of a 5-7 slide talk. Aim for a clear spoken explanation of the audience, question, data, main finding, and limitation — not a read-aloud of every word on the slides.

## Slide Submission

Before the portfolio deadline, commit and sync:

```text
milestones/m5-presentation/submission/slides.qmd
milestones/m5-presentation/submission/slides.html
```

If you render to PDF instead of HTML, submit `slides.pdf`. Commit the narrated recording alongside them. Submit the GitHub repository link on Canvas with the latest commit hash and the slide path.

<!-- AI-EDIT(2026-06-11): TF-039, MIT-108, WI-062 — needs review -->
::: {.callout-note title="What is a commit hash?"}
A commit hash is the unique identifier GitHub assigns every saved version of your work. It looks like `a3f92bc`. To find it, go to your repository on GitHub, click **Commits**, and copy the short code on the right. You can also run `git log --oneline -1` in the terminal.
:::

## Slide Checklist

Before submitting, check that:

- slides render from source in a fresh Codespace;
- fonts and figures are readable on screen;
- every chart has a title, units, and limitation cue;
- source and data notes are visible;
- the final slide gives the audience a clear takeaway;
- the narration is audible and matches what is on screen;
- backup notes include data source, cohort, and AI-use details.

## Portfolio Reminder

The presentation is scored as the **Presentation** component (10 points) of the Final Portfolio. Use the M4 peer feedback you received to revise the final report, dashboard-style KT product, and deck together, then confirm the [Final Portfolio Checklist](../../milestones/final-portfolio/final-portfolio-checklist.md) before submission.

## Definition Of Done

The presentation is done when the narrated slides are committed, rendered, and submitted with the Final Portfolio, and play without relying on local-only files.
